thread:
Devon Lee: quick one — during the AP-SG canary I'm seeing short 429 spikes and a handful of 422s for acme on route=/api/v1/generate (model=gen). Anyone have a compact saved search or one-liner to drop into LogSearch? Need something I can share in the canary playbook.

Jia Chen: @Devon Lee I made a small saved view for exactly this a while back. URL: https://internal.redwood/logs/saved/views/acme-ap-sg-gen-errors-quick

Jia Chen: Starter query (uses field names we index):
```
_tags.prod:true AND org_id:acme AND region:ap-sg AND route:"/api/v1/generate" AND (status_code:422 OR status_code:429)
| parse field=model_name "*" as model
| where model=="gen"
| timechart span=1m count() by status_code, host
```

Devon Lee: nice, thanks. Can you add a per-host top20 breakdown too? Want to see if a single instance is noisy.

Jia Chen: added inline to the saved view. Extra snippet: 
```
| stats count() by host, status_code
| sort -count
| limit 20
```

Maria Gomez: Grafana link that helps correlate infra metrics: https://grafana.redwood/d/infra-routing (panel: "Route errors & host CPU"). If the host shows >40% CPU when errors spike that's a hint it might be backpressure.

Maria Gomez: Current alert is route_error_rate-ap-sg: fires when errors > 6/min for 1m. That's noisy for short canary spikes. Proposal: change to trigger when errors >= 10 across 3m OR when error_rate sustained > 4/min for 5m. Also, add a label canary_id so we can silence known canaries.

Sam Patel: +1 on using a stability window. My suggested rule: (count(status_code=429) >= 10 AND increase_rate > 2x baseline) over 3m. Baseline = previous 30m rolling. That helps catch sudden regressions vs normal bumpiness. We can also auto-suppress alerts if rollout_tag=canary.

Devon Lee: ops-bot posted an alert earlier that matched our window — saved that incident. ops-bot, can you paste the alert payload here for reference?

ops-bot: [Alert] 2026-05-18T14:12:07Z — route_error_rate-ap-sg triggered; org=acme route=/api/v1/generate status=429 count=14 rollout_tag=canary-20260518

Devon Lee: that lines up exactly with our canary window. I'll move the saved view into the canary troubleshooting playbook at /docs/playbooks/canary-troubleshooting.md so oncall has it preloaded.

Jia Chen: done — added the saved view link, the per-host snippet, and two quick grep queries for 422 root causes (invalid payload vs tokenization failures).

Jia Chen: 422 helper queries I put in the playbook: 
```
org_id:acme region:ap-sg route:"/api/v1/generate" status_code:422
| stats count() by error_message
| where error_message like "%invalid_payload%" OR error_message like "%tokenization_error%"
```

Maria Gomez: I'll open a tiny PR in ops-alerting to add the 3m/5m options and include rollout_tag filtering. Will mark it for quick review and include a note about auto-silencing canaries for 30m windows.

Sam Patel: I'll review the PR and run it in staging for 24 hours. If noise drops and we still catch real regressions we'll promote.

Devon Lee: one final ask — can we add a dashboard panel that shows recent saved views hits (so we can audit how often folks are checking these during canary)? small UX win.

Maria Gomez: good idea. I'll add a Grafana panel that queries LogSearch meta for saved view hits and show it on infra/routing.

Devon Lee: thanks all — closing this thread. If new patterns pop up (specific error_message values) I'll reopen. :thumbsup:
